text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer notes the AMG EQE out-muscles the i5 M60 (617 hp, up to 677 hp in race start; 0-100 km/h 3.5 vs 3.8 s), its main advantage in the test. Reviewer states the AMG EQE's adaptive suspension feels firm at all times, while the i5's comfort-mode ride is far better. Reviewer finds the AMG EQE's steering artificially heavy and favours the i5 on handling. Reviewer finds the AMG EQE's brake feel inconsistent. Reviewer finds the EQE's many small steering-wheel controls and dash-wide screen overwhelming at first, while praising the i5's simpler layout. Reviewer calls neither cabin elegant but rates the i5's finishes top-notch, favouring BMW on interior. Reviewer states the EQE's rear seat has scant headroom and squat windows that feel claustrophobic, while the i5's rear is notably roomier. Reviewer notes the i5's trunk holds 60 litres more, although the EQE's rear seatbacks fold electrically. Reviewer reports negative feedback on the EQE's styling, with one editor saying it looked like it was melting; the i5's styling is preferred. Reviewer notes the AMG EQE uses more energy (3.2 vs 2.6 Le/100 km) and has less rated range (362 vs 399 km) than the i5 M60. Reviewer notes the AMG EQE's 170 kW peak DC charging rate trails the i5's 205 kW. Reviewer calls the i5's value advantage dramatic: the AMG EQE starts at C$121,500 versus C$95,000 for the i5 M60. Reviewer scores the AMG EQE and i5 M60 equally (9/10) on safety. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «always feels firm» «artificially heavy»
